source_residual.source_authority: R47I frozen genuine_residual_fixpoint and R50G25X artifact 9992845123

Q_HORN.method: Exact finite ternary valuation replay using the same q-Horn condition frozen in JANUS R39; 22 search nodes after pruning.

BETA_ACYCLIC.method: Nest-point elimination characterization; no initial nest point exists.

strong_2cnf_backdoor.minimality_method: Exhaustive subset check over the 20 variables using the deletion characterization for strong 2-CNF backdoors: deleting the chosen variables must leave every clause with width <=2. No subset of size <7 satisfies the condition.
strong_2cnf_backdoor.public_theory: Strong backdoor detection to 2-CNF is fixed-parameter tractable; Horn/2-CNF have the deletion property.
strong_2cnf_backdoor.meaning: This historical JANUS controller-stall is not outside all known exact methods. A standard public backdoor lane can recognize/solve it when parameterized by k=7.
not_meaning: All R50 residuals have logarithmic/small backdoors.
The minimum backdoor remains O(log N) on any infinite hard family.
Backdoor search is polynomial for unbounded k.

independent_sat_replay.backdoor_assignment_search: Enumerated assignments to the seven backdoor variables; for each assignment the residual is <=2CNF.

scientific_interpretation.historical_lesson: The old strict-descent controller failed because its grammar omitted a known parameterized route; the residual itself should not be treated as evidence that a new local reduction rule was necessary.
scientific_interpretation.portfolio_lesson: Before inventing a successor rule for a stalled residual, run exact recognizers/parameter detectors for known public lanes.
scientific_interpretation.universal_lesson: A single finite small-backdoor case closes only this residual. The universal target remains a FOR-ALL theorem that every residual has a polynomially discoverable small parameter/lane or a polynomial controlled-growth funnel into one.

references: Nishimura, Ragde, Szeider, Detecting Backdoor Sets with Respect to Horn and Binary Clauses, SAT 2004.
Boros, Hammer, Sun, Recognition of q-Horn formulae in linear time, Discrete Applied Mathematics 55(1), 1994.
Ordyniak, Paulusma, Szeider, Satisfiability of acyclic and almost acyclic CNF formulas, Theoretical Computer Science 481, 2013.
